=== bar-bordercolor-large-data ===
title: 'fix(bar): fix borderColor hides bar color with large data'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Large bar-series rendering can lose the bar fill when `borderColor` is configured, making bars appear incorrectly outlined or visually empty. This is especially noticeable in dense charts where the large-data path is chosen automatically.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix the large-data bar rendering path so `borderColor` does not hide the bar’s actual fill color.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars rendered through the large-data path keep their fill color even when `borderColor` is set, border styling still applies as expected, and standard bar rendering remains unchanged.'
=== calendar-label-silent ===
title: 'feat(calendar): add `silent` option for `dayLabel`/`monthLabel`/`yearLabel`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using the calendar coordinate system may want the day, month, or year labels to serve as static annotation rather than interactive elements. Today those labels still participate in pointer interaction, which can interfere with hover behavior on the actual calendar data and make embedded dashboards feel unexpectedly clickable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calendar label interaction should be configurable independently for `dayLabel`, `monthLabel`, and `yearLabel`. When a user sets `silent: true` on any of those label configs, the corresponding rendered text should ignore pointer events while preserving the existing visual styling and positioning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can set `dayLabel.silent`, `monthLabel.silent`, and `yearLabel.silent` directly in the calendar option, and each one takes effect on its own. With `silent: true`, the label remains visible but no longer behaves like an interactive graphic element; with the option omitted or false, existing behavior stays unchanged.

  '
=== custom-renderitem-compoundpath ===
title: 'feat(custom): support compoundPath in custom series renderItem'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Custom-series authors sometimes need to return a composed path made from several subpaths as a single logical drawing element. Today `compoundPath` is not supported in `renderItem`, which blocks reusable vector shapes that are straightforward in lower-level graphics APIs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Support `compoundPath` as a valid custom-series element type so `renderItem` can return grouped path geometry in one element definition, provided `shape.paths` is supplied.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A custom series can return a `compoundPath` element from `renderItem`, `shape.paths` is honored when constructing the final graphic, and invalid compound definitions still fail clearly instead of silently misrendering.'
=== dark-legend-page-text ===
title: 'fix(theme): fix legend page text color in dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, legend pagination text can retain an incorrect color that reduces contrast and readability against the theme background. Users experience this as a theme inconsistency in otherwise polished dark dashboards.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix dark-theme legend page text coloring so paged legends remain readable and visually consistent with the rest of the dark theme.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Legend page text in dark mode uses an appropriate readable color, pagination controls stay visible against the dark background, and light-theme behavior is unchanged.'
=== geojson-region-styling ===
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams who maintain their own GeoJSON files often want the map source itself to carry default presentation rules for specific regions, instead of forcing every chart option to restate those styles. At the moment, styling embedded directly in the GeoJSON is ignored, which makes shared map assets harder to reuse across multiple visualizations.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a GeoJSON region includes an `echartsStyle` property in its feature properties, ECharts should treat that as the region''s default styling for geo rendering. This should let authors ship map-specific visual defaults inside the original GeoJSON while still allowing chart configuration to build on top of those defaults where appropriate.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Region-level styles declared in GeoJSON `properties.echartsStyle` are reflected when the map is rendered through geo-based views, without requiring duplicate style configuration in every chart option. Existing GeoJSON files that do not define `echartsStyle` continue to render exactly as before.

  '

=== geojson-region-styling-2 ===
title: 'feat(geo): support styling region in original GeoJSON data'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors need region defaults embedded in GeoJSON to work consistently whether they use a standalone `geo` component or a `series.map`, and whether or not they explicitly list every region in `data` or `regions`. The initial GeoJSON styling support still leaves gaps in those map-series flows, especially when a region only exists in the source map and not in user-supplied series data.

  ## Desired outcome

  GeoJSON-defined region styling should become a first-class default across map usage, not just a geo-view special case. If a feature provides `properties.echartsStyle`, that style should flow into both `geo.regions` and `series.map` region models, including regions that need to be synthesized into the data so name-based lookup, rendering, and labels all remain complete.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A `series.map` can pick up `properties.echartsStyle` from the original GeoJSON even when the author did not manually add a matching data item for that region. The style participates in the normal region model pipeline instead of being a one-off view patch, so map rendering, labels, and region lookup stay consistent with other region options.

  '
=== map-regions-silent ===
title: 'feat(map): support `regions[].silent` and update map data in tests'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Map authors sometimes need a region to remain visible but non-interactive, for example when a background territory should not respond to hover, selection, or tooltip behavior. ECharts already supports top-level `silent` behavior, but there is no reliable per-region contract for map and geo regions, so authors cannot selectively disable interaction on individual areas.

  ## Desired outcome

  Region configuration should support `silent` at the per-region level through `regions[].silent`, and that setting should be honored for both geo-based maps and `series.map` rendering. A region marked silent should keep its visual appearance while opting out of event handling and interactive affordances, without forcing the entire map to become non-interactive.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Authors can declare `silent` on individual entries in `regions`, and the targeted region becomes non-interactive while neighboring regions continue to respond normally. The contract applies consistently to rendered GeoJSON regions and SVG-backed regions, and map data refreshes should preserve the updated region behavior instead of losing it when the source map data changes.

  '
=== markline-symboloffset-2d-array ===
title: 'fix(type): markLine `symbolOffset` can be a 2d array for both symbols'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users configuring mark lines may want separate offsets for the symbols at each end, but the current type definition can reject valid configurations even though the renderer supports them. This creates unnecessary friction in strongly typed projects.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the public type contract so markLine `symbolOffset` accepts a 2D array when authors need to specify offsets for both symbols independently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  TypeScript accepts markLine configurations where `symbolOffset` is expressed as separate offset pairs for the two end symbols, existing simpler `symbolOffset` forms remain valid, and runtime chart behavior is unchanged.'
=== master-into-v6 ===
title: 'chore: merge master into v6'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The v6 release branch needs regular synchronization with ongoing master development so maintainers can keep packaging, fixes, and infrastructure aligned. This is branch-management work, not a new user-visible feature.


  ## Desired outcome

  Merge the relevant master changes into the v6 branch while preserving the expected public behavior of the release line and avoiding regressions introduced by branch drift.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The v6 branch reflects the intended upstream updates, the merge does not invent a new standalone feature requirement of its own, and user-facing behavior is whatever the merged source already defines.'
=== pictorial-zero-value-flipping ===
title: 'fix(pictorial): fix zero value flipping for different axes'

title: 'fix(sankey): avoid throwing errors when the `links` / `nodes` / `levels` option is undefined'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Applications sometimes build sankey options incrementally, and optional arrays such as `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` may be undefined until later. ECharts should not crash just because those optional fields are temporarily absent.


  ## Desired outcome

  Handle missing sankey `links`, `nodes`, and `levels` inputs defensively so the chart no longer throws when those option fields are undefined.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A sankey option with undefined `links`, `nodes`, or `levels` no longer raises an exception, normal sankey rendering still works when those arrays are provided, and authors do not need to add dummy empty arrays solely to avoid crashes.'

title: 'fix(data): fix potential NPE in the `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` function'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A developer using ECharts internals or extension code can end up calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` in situations where the requested dimension does not have an inverted index. Instead of failing gracefully, that lookup can crash the chart pipeline with a null-pointer style error before the caller has any chance to recover.

  ## Desired outcome

  `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` should be safe to call even when the requested dimension is missing from the inverted-index map. In that case it should behave like an unsuccessful lookup rather than a hard failure, so downstream code can continue handling the result normally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling `SeriesData#rawIndexOf` with a dimension that has no inverted index must not throw in production execution. The method should return the same "not found" result it already uses for missing values, namely `INDEX_NOT_FOUND`, so callers see a consistent contract instead of an exception.

  '

title: 'feat(sunburst): add new emphasis focus strategy `''relative''` for highlighting ancestor and descendant nodes'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Add a new sunburst emphasis focus mode named `relative` so hovering or emphasizing a node can highlight its surrounding family context, including both ancestor and descendant nodes, in one built-in strategy.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting the sunburst emphasis focus strategy to `relative` highlights the target node together with its ancestors and descendants, other focus strategies keep their current semantics, and charts that do not use the new mode are unchanged.'

title: 'fix(tooltip): Tooltip textStyle lineHeight does not work in default '

requirement: '## Context

title: 'fix(tooltip): fix potential NPE when setting option with `notMerge` strategy'

requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Make tooltip HTML handling resilient when options are replaced with `notMerge`, so rerendering does not trigger a null-pointer-style failure during size or position updates.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling `setOption` with `notMerge` no longer crashes tooltip logic, tooltip positioning still works after rerender, and unaffected tooltip behavior remains unchanged.'

title: 'fix(visualMap): fix cursor is still pointer when `selectedMode` is disabled'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A dashboard author can configure a piecewise visualMap as read-only by setting `selectedMode: false`, for example when the legend-like scale is meant to explain colors without filtering data. Right now the control still advertises itself as clickable: hovering its pieces shows a pointer cursor even though clicking does nothing, which is misleading in polished analytical UIs.

  ## Desired outcome

  A piecewise visualMap with `selectedMode: false` should behave as a non-interactive display element, not as a disabled button that still looks active. Its symbols and labels should stop presenting click affordances while the normal selectable modes continue to behave exactly as they do today.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `selectedMode` is enabled, hovering the visualMap still shows the interactive cursor and selection behavior is unchanged. When `selectedMode: false`, the rendered pieces and their labels no longer expose a pointer cursor and should behave as silent display content rather than clickable controls.

  '
